description:
Most people still think “cloud” means Google Drive, but the reality is way bigger: companies now run almost everything on cloud platforms instead of on‑premise servers, powering a multi‑hundred‑billion‑dollar industry. In this conversational breakdown, you’ll hear how over 90% of enterprises already rely on cloud services and often cut 30–40% of their IT costs by doing so, with AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud leading the market. We also unpack what’s new in 2026: AI built directly into cloud tools so teams can add LLMs and analytics without managing their own infrastructure, edge computing that processes data closer to users for lower latency, and multi‑cloud strategies so businesses aren’t locked into a single provider. By the end, you’ll see why modern cloud is less about “online storage” and more about where entire products, apps, and AI systems actually live and run.

author: Simplilearn
description:
In this quick video, we’re diving into the key differences between a Fullstack Developer and a Backend Developer!  Whether you're new to tech or considering a career shift, understanding these roles is crucial.

A Fullstack Developer handles both the frontend and backend, mastering HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Node.js, while also working with databases and server-side technologies. They ensure everything works together smoothly from the user interface to server management.

On the other hand, a Backend Developer focuses on server-side development. They work with databases (like MySQL or MongoDB) and server-side languages like Java, Ruby, or Python. Their job is to ensure data flow, security, and the functionality behind the scenes.

So, if you’re considering a career as a Fullstack Developer or a Backend Developer, understanding their key responsibilities will help you make the right decision. Watch till the end for more insights on which role is the best fit for you in 2026! 💻🚀
